- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for next 3–7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter: average last 5 days’ sentiment to weight next forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model may misread trend; use sentiment median as anchor for 7–14 day forecast.
